en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-akṣamālā-sūtra*, translated by an unknown person, now appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was traveling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with...
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus and countless bodhisattvas whose fame was renowned afar and who were revered by devas and humans.
At that time, King Pāyāsi of the kingdom of Kāśi sent an envoy to the Buddha’s presence; he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

My country is small and remote, yet for many years it has been plagued by bandits and rebels; the five grains have become exceedingly expensive, diseases spread everywhere, and the people suffer in misery, so that I can never lie down in peace.
The Dharma-treasury of the Tathāgata is for the most part profound and vast;
I have many concerns and duties, and thus am unable to practice.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will specially bestow his compassionate pity upon me and grant me the essential Dharma!
"May it enable me to practice easily day and night, so that in future lives I may remain far removed from all suffering.
The Buddha told the king:
"If you wish to extinguish the hindrance of afflictions and the hindrance of retribution, you should string together one hundred and eight wood nut seeds (mbu-kaṇḍa) and always carry them with you."

Whether walking, sitting, or lying down, one should always maintain a sincere mind without distraction, reciting the names of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṃgha while passing each wood nut (*bhallātaka*). In this manner, one gradually passes the wood nuts—whether ten, twenty, a hundred, a thousand, or even hundreds of thousands, millions, and tens of millions.

If one can complete two hundred thousand recitations with body and mind undistracted and free from all deceit and crookedness, upon the end of life, one will be reborn in the third heaven, the Yāma Heaven, where food and clothing appear spontaneously and one always dwells in peace and happiness.

If one can further complete one million recitations, one shall succeed in severing the hundred-and-eight fetters of karma; this is truly called turning one's back on the stream of birth and death and heading toward Nirvana, forever cutting off the roots of affliction and attaining the unsurpassed fruit.
Śraddhā returned and informed the king; the king was greatly delighted and, facing the World-Honored One from afar, prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha's feet, saying:
"Excellent! I shall respectfully practice it."
He immediately issued a decree to the officials and commoners to prepare *mukūlaka* seeds, making one thousand sets; each of his six types of relatives and state kinsmen was given one set.
The King constantly recited and contemplated them, never ceasing even when personally engaged in military campaigns.
He further thought:
"The World-Honored One is of great compassion and universally responds to all.
If this merit of mine allows me to escape long submersion in the sea of suffering, the Tathāgata should manifest before my very eyes and preach the Dharma for me."
His longing and aspiration pressed upon his heart, and for three days he did not eat.
The Buddha immediately manifested his form, accompanied by his retinue, and came into the king’s palace, where he addressed the king, saying:
“The bhikṣu Śāḍva recited the names of the Triple Gem for ten years and attained the fruit of a Sakṛdāgāmin.”
"By practicing gradually, he now dwells in the world of Universal Fragrance as a pratyekabuddha.
Having heard this, the king redoubled his practice.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"How much more so for those who can recite the names of the Triple Gem ten thousand times!
Even those who merely hear the name of this person and give rise to a single thought of sympathetic joy will, in their future births, constantly hear of the ten wholesome paths of action."
When this Dharma was spoken, the great assembly rejoiced and all vowed to practice it accordingly.
Thus ends the *Buddha-bhāṣita-akṣamālā-sūtra*.
